about: Ground truth for the four field rooms, as read from each panorama by eye (camera height, door heights, floor and ceiling lines). Treat sizes as ±10%, not tape-measured. Plan coordinates are metres, origin at the room centre, x toward Wall 2, y toward Wall 3; items are [label, x, y, width, depth, kind] with kind f=floor piece, w=wall piece, x=not furniture (column, opening), r=rug.

slicing.yawNote: wallYawDeg is the panorama yaw (0 = centre column, positive = turn right) each wall photo is cut at; Walls 1-4 run clockwise.

rooms.name: Empty apartment room

walls.name: Balcony
walls.note: A glazed balcony door with dark curtains drawn to both sides. The AC unit sits high on the left.

walls.name: Plain wall
walls.note: An empty wall with a single socket. The right result here is nothing at all.

walls.name: Entry
walls.note: An interior door on the left. The papered block is a boxed-in column standing out about 0.8 m, not a piece of furniture.

walls.name: Side wall
walls.note: Papered column on the right, then sockets. The AC from Wall 1 shows again at the top-right corner: it should not become a second unit.

watch: Does Wall 3 come out at the box's face (about 4.4 m deep) or at the door behind it (about 5.2 m)? Danmu assumes four flat walls.
Wall 2 should stay empty. A false find on a blank wall is worth noting.

rooms.name: Hotel room

walls.name: Window
walls.note: A full window with sheer and grey curtains. A yellow armchair in the left corner and two pendant lamps.

walls.name: Bed
walls.note: A double bed recessed in a dark wardrobe alcove, with wall reading lights and a long mirror.

walls.name: Entry
walls.note: A frosted bathroom door and the entry door, with a framed print between them.

walls.name: TV & desk
walls.note: A wall-mounted TV over a long desk with an office chair. The armchair from Wall 1 shows at the right edge.

watch: The camera is 0.4 m closer to Wall 4, so Wall 2 pieces read slightly small and Wall 4 pieces slightly large.
The bed's head is about 0.5 m behind the wall line (the alcove). Watch whether the bed is pushed into the room.
The armchair appears in Walls 1 and 4. It should come out as one chair.

rooms.name: Seaview suite

walls.name: Balcony
walls.note: Sliding balcony doors with curtains. A wall TV over a bar fridge and microwave on the left. A lantern chandelier, and the bed's corner at the right edge.

walls.name: Bed
walls.note: Double bed between two nightstands with lamps, three prints above, an AC unit high up. A wicker chest at the foot, a door at the far right.

walls.name: Wardrobe
walls.note: A built-in wardrobe, the entry door and a round mirror, plus an armchair with a pedestal table and plant. The chaise starts at the right.

walls.name: Desk
walls.note: A chaise longue under a clock, then a desk with chair, lamp and kettle tray, and a wall mirror. The TV wall starts at the right.

watch: The chaise is in Walls 3 and 4, and the TV/fridge corner in Walls 1 and 4. Each should be built once.
The wardrobe is built into the wall, about 0.6 m deep. It should sit against Wall 3, not stand in the room.
Small table-top things (kettle, clock, vases) are not in the catalogue. Ignoring them is correct.

rooms.name: Family lounge

walls.name: Window
walls.note: A window with a valance, a dark sideboard to the left and the start of the green sectional on the right.

walls.name: Sofa
walls.note: The long side of the corner sofa, a glass coffee table, a painting and shelves of books and plants.

walls.name: Hatch
walls.note: An opening through to the next room, another sofa module, an armchair, a low wooden table and pictures.

walls.name: Second window
walls.note: A second window with a valance, a green armchair and the same flower cabinet seen in Wall 1.

watch: Danmu assumes a camera at 1.5 m. Here it is about 1.0 m, so expect distances, and the sizes that come from them, to read about a third too large. This is the most useful failure case in the kit.
The sectional turns the corner between Walls 1 and 2. One L-shaped sofa, or two sofas, is the honest answer. Three would be a duplicate.
The cabinet appears in Walls 1 and 4. It should be built once.
